chapterNote: The third of the seven penitential psalms, and the one that completes the set for this translation. Its title is a single word — le-hazkir, 'to bring to remembrance' — and what it brings to remembrance is a body. David asks God not to rebuke him in wrath, and then describes what the wrath has already done: arrows sunk in, a hand pressing down, no soundness in the flesh, no peace in the bones, iniquities gone over his head like water and too heavy to carry, wounds that stink because of his own folly, loins on fire, a heart pounding, the light of his eyes gone. Around the sickbed the human world empties out: friends and neighbors stand back from the stroke, kinsmen keep their distance, and the men who want him dead lay snares and rehearse lies all day. His answer to them is silence — he becomes a deaf man who does not hear, a mute man with no rebuttal in his mouth — because his case is not with them: in You, O LORD, I hope; You will answer, O Lord my God. Then the one sentence the whole psalm has been moving toward: I will declare my iniquity; I am anxious over my sin. It ends with three short cries, and the last word is salvation.

1.text: A psalm of David, to bring to remembrance. O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your wrath, and do not discipline me in Your burning anger.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of David, to bring to remembrance [zakar]. O LORD [YHWH], rebuke [yakach] me not in Your wrath [qetseph]: neither chasten [yasar — discipline] me in Your hot displeasure [chemah — burning fury].
1.notes: le-hazkir (H2142): 'to bring to remembrance' — the one-word title, shared with Psalm 70; the same root as the memorial portion of the grain offering (Leviticus 2:2), so the psalm is itself an offering laid before God. YHWH al-be-qetsppekha tokhicheni (H3068, H7110, H3198): not in Your wrath — u-ba-chamatekha teyassereni (H2534, H3256): not in Your burning fury. He does not ask to escape the rebuke or the discipline, only to have them come from love rather than fury (cf. Psalm 6:1, the same opening; Jeremiah 10:24). The third of the church's seven penitential psalms.

2.text: For Your arrows have sunk into me, and Your hand has come down hard on me.
2.amp: For Your arrows [chets] stick fast in me, and Your hand [yad] presses me sore.
2.notes: ki-chitsekha nichatu bi (H2671, H5181): for Your ARROWS have come down into me — the arrows of Job 6:4, whose poison the spirit drinks; va-tinchat alai yadekha (H3027): and Your hand has descended on me. The same verb twice, arrows and hand: whatever is happening to his body, David reads it as coming from God, and says so before he says anything else.

3.text: There is no soundness in my flesh because of Your indignation; there is no peace in my bones because of my sin.
3.amp: There is no soundness in my flesh [basar] because [panim] of Your anger; neither is there any rest ['peace, or, health', shalom, the KJV margin] in my bones [etsem] because [panim] of my sin [chattath].
3.notes: en-metom bi-bsari mi-pene zaamekha (H1320, H6440): no metom — no sound spot — in my flesh, from the face of Your indignation; en-shalom ba-atsamai mi-pene chattati (H7965, H6106, H2403): no shalom in my bones, the margin's 'peace, or, health', from the face of my sin. Two faces named as causes: God's anger and David's sin, and the psalm never separates them.

4.text: For my iniquities have gone over my head; like a heavy load they are too heavy for me.
4.amp: For mine iniquities [avon] are gone over [abar] mine head [rosh]: as an heavy burden [massa] they are too heavy [kabad] for me.
4.notes: ki-avonotai aberu roshi (H5771, H5674, H7218): my iniquities have PASSED OVER my head — the flood-image of Psalm 69:2, guilt as water closing above a man; ke-massa khabed yikhbedu mimmenni (H4853, H3513): like a heavy massa, a load, they are heavier than I am. Guilt weighed rather than counted (cf. Matthew 11:28, where the load is offered to Someone else).

5.text: My wounds stink and fester because of my own foolishness.
5.amp: My wounds [chaburah — stripes] stink [baash] and are corrupt because [panim] of my foolishness [ivvelet].
5.notes: hibishu namaqqu chaburotai (H887, H4743, H2250): my chaburot — the welts of a beating, the same word Isaiah 53:5 uses of the stripes that heal us — stink and run; mi-pene ivvalti (H6440, H200): from the face of my ivvelet, my folly. He names the cause without excuse: not fate, not enemies, foolishness. The Physician is not spared the smell.

6.text: I am bent over and bowed down very low; all day long I go about in mourning.
6.amp: I am troubled ['wried', avah, the KJV margin]; I am bowed down [shachah] greatly [meod]; I go [halak] mourning [qadar] all the day [yom] long.
6.notes: naaveti shachoti ad-meod (H5753, H7817, H3966): I am bent — the margin's 'wried', twisted out of shape — I am bowed down VERY; kol-ha-yom qoder hillakhti (H3117, H6937, H1980): all the day I have walked about qoder, in the dark clothes of a mourner, the word of Psalm 43:2. A man doubled over, going nowhere in particular.

7.text: For my loins are full of a scorching fire, and no part of my flesh is sound.
7.amp: For my loins are filled [male] with a loathsome disease: and there is no soundness in my flesh [basar].
7.notes: ki-khesalai maleu niqleh (H4390, H7033): my loins are full of a burning — the KJV's 'loathsome disease', the WEB's 'burning'; the root is to roast or scorch; ve-en metom bi-bsari (H1320): and no sound spot in my flesh, verse 3's refrain returning. The psalm never names the illness, which is why every sick believer has been able to use it.

8.text: I am numb and crushed to the last degree; I have roared from the groaning of my heart.
8.amp: I am feeble and sore [meod] broken: I have roared by reason of the disquietness [nehamah — groaning] of my heart [leb].
8.notes: nephugoti ve-nidketi ad-meod (H6313, H1794): I am gone numb and CRUSHED to the utmost — daka, Psalm 51:8's broken bones; shaagti mi-nahamat libbi (H7580, H5100, H3820): I have ROARED from my heart's groaning — shaag, the lion's roar of Psalm 22:1, here coming out of a sickbed. Pain past the reach of words takes the shape of an animal.

9.text: Lord, all my longing is in front of You, and my sighing is not hidden from You.
9.amp: Lord [Adonai], all my desire [taavah] is before You; and my groaning [anachah] is not hid [satar] from You.
9.notes: Adonai negdekha khol-taavati (H136, H8378): Lord — Adonai, Master — all my taavah, my longing, is right in front of You; ve-anchati mimmekha lo-nistarah (H585, H5641): and my sighing is not hidden from You. The one comfort in the first half of the psalm: the groaning he cannot explain to his friends needs no explaining here (cf. Romans 8:26).

10.text: My heart pounds, my strength has left me, and the light of my eyes — even that is gone from me.
10.amp: My heart [leb] pants, my strength [koach] fails [azab — has left] me: as for the light [or] of mine eyes [ayin], it also is gone ['is not with me', ayin, the KJV margin] from me.
10.notes: libbi secharchar azabani khochi (H3820, H5503, H5800, H3581): my heart goes round and round — the doubled form for a racing pulse — my strength has ABANDONED me; ve-or enai gam-hem en itti (H216, H5869): and the light of my eyes, even they are 'not with me', the margin's literal. The last thing to go is the light in the eyes, which is the Hebrew way of saying the life (cf. 1 Samuel 14:27).

11.text: My loved ones and my friends stand back from my affliction, and my near ones stand far off.
11.amp: My lovers [ahab] and my friends [rea] stand [amad] aloof from [neged] my sore ['stroke', nega, the KJV margin]; and my kinsmen ['my neighbours', qarov, the KJV margin] stand [amad] afar off [rachoq].
11.notes: ohabai ve-reai mi-neged nigi yaamodu (H157, H7453, H5061): my lovers and my friends stand off from my nega — the margin's 'stroke', the word for the priest's leprosy examination (Leviticus 13:3): they treat him as contagious. u-qerobai me-rachoq amadu (H7138, H7350): and my near ones — qarov, the very word for 'near' — stood far off. Job's friends, and the crowd at a certain cross (Luke 23:49).

12.text: Those who seek my life set traps; those who want my ruin speak of destruction and mutter deceit all day long.
12.amp: They also that seek [baqash] after my life [nephesh] lay snares for me: and they that seek [darash] my hurt [ra] speak [dabar] mischievous things [havvah — destruction], and imagine [hagah — mutter] deceits [mirmah] all the day [yom] long.
12.notes: va-yenaqshu mebaqshe naphshi (H5367, H1245, H5315): the seekers of my life set snares. ve-doreshe raati dibberu havvot (H1875, H7451, H1696, H1942): the seekers of my harm speak havvot, ruinous things. u-mirmot kol-ha-yom yehgu (H4820, H3117, H1897): and deceits all the day they MUTTER — hagah, the meditation-verb of Psalm 1:2, aimed the other way: they rehearse their lies the way the blessed man rehearses the law.

13.text: But I am like a deaf man who does not hear, like a mute who does not open his mouth.
13.amp: But I, as a deaf man, heard [shama] not; and I was as a dumb man [illem] that opens [pathach] not his mouth [peh].
13.notes: va-ani khe-cheresh lo eshma (H2795, H8085): but I, like a deaf man, do not hear — u-khe-illem lo yiphtach-piv (H483, H6605, H6310): and like a mute who does not open his mouth. Not the silence of a man with nothing to say but of one who has decided not to answer — Isaiah 53:7's lamb, and 1 Peter 2:23's 'when he was reviled, reviled not again'.

14.text: So I became like a man who does not hear, and in whose mouth there are no rebuttals.
14.amp: Thus I was as a man [ish] that hears [shama] not, and in whose mouth [peh] are no reproofs [tokachat — rebuttals].
14.notes: va-ehi ke-ish asher lo-shomea (H376): I became like a man who does not hear; ve-en be-phiv tokhachot (H6310, H8433): and in his mouth are no tokhachot — arguments, counter-charges. He has none, because on the main point his accusers are right: he has sinned (v. 18). The silence is honest, not tactical.

15.text: For in You, O LORD, I have hoped; You Yourself will answer, O Lord my God.
15.amp: For in You ['thee do I wait for', yachal, the KJV margin], O LORD [YHWH], do I hope [yachal]: You will hear ['answer', anah, the KJV margin], O Lord [Adonai] my God [Elohim].
15.notes: ki-lekha YHWH hochalti (H3068, H3176): for it is for YOU, LORD, that I have waited — yachal, hope as waiting, the margin's 'wait for'; attah taaneh Adonai Elohai (H6030, H136, H430): YOU will answer, Adonai my God — the margin's 'answer'. The reason for the silence of verses 13-14: he is saving his voice for the only court that matters.

16.text: For I said, 'Let them not gloat over me, who magnify themselves against me when my foot slips.'
16.amp: For I said [amar], Hear me, lest otherwise they should rejoice [samach] over me: when my foot [regel] slips [mot], they magnify [gadal] themselves against me.
16.notes: ki-amarti pen-yismechu-li (H559, H8055): for I said, lest they rejoice over me — be-mot ragli alai higdilu (H4131, H7272, H1431): when my foot slips they MAGNIFY themselves over me — gadal, the same verb Psalm 41:9 uses of the heel lifted against him. A slip is all his enemies are waiting for, and he knows how close he is to one (v. 17).

17.text: For I am ready to fall, and my pain is in front of me continually.
17.amp: For I am ready [kun] to halt ['for halting', tsela, the KJV margin], and my sorrow [makob — pain] is continually [tamid] before me.
17.notes: ki-ani le-tsela nakhon (H6761, H3559): for I am SET for stumbling — 'ready for halting', the margin's literal: prepared, poised, one step from the fall; u-makobi negdi tamid (H4341, H8548): and my pain is in front of me continually — tamid, the word for the daily burnt offering: pain as a standing appointment.

18.text: For I declare my iniquity; I am anxious over my sin.
18.amp: For I will declare [nagad] mine iniquity [avon]; I will be sorry for my sin [chattath].
18.notes: ki-avoni aggid (H5771, H5046): for my iniquity I DECLARE — nagad, to tell out in the open, the same verb used of announcing news; eddag me-chattati (H1672, H2403): I am anxious over my sin — daag, the worry-word of Jeremiah 17:8's tree that has no care in drought. The turn the whole psalm has been moving toward: not 'I am ill' but 'I have sinned', said out loud (cf. Psalm 32:5; 1 John 1:9).

19.text: But my enemies are full of life and strong, and those who hate me for nothing have multiplied.
19.amp: But mine enemies [oyeb] are lively ['being living, are strong', chay, the KJV margin], and they are strong [atsam]: and they that hate [sane] me wrongfully [sheqer] are multiplied.
19.notes: ve-oyebai chayyim atsemu (H341, H2416, H6105): my enemies are ALIVE and grown mighty — the margin's 'being living, are strong': while he wastes, they thrive; ve-rabbu soneai shaqer (H7231, H8130, H8267): and my haters, sheqer — falsely, for a lie — are many. The line Jesus applies to Himself in John 15:25, 'they hated me without a cause'.

20.text: Those who repay evil for good oppose me, because I pursue what is good.
20.amp: They also that render [shalam — repay] evil [ra] for good [tov] are mine adversaries [satan]; because I follow [radaph — pursue] the thing that good [tov] is.
20.notes: u-meshallme raah tachat tovah yistenuni (H7999, H7451, H2896, H7853): repayers of evil for good OPPOSE me — the verb is satan, to act as an adversary, the noun behind the accuser's name (Job 1:6; Zechariah 3:1); tachat rodphi-tov (H7291): in return for my PURSUING good. Being hated for doing right is its own category of grief (cf. 1 Peter 3:17).

21.text: Do not abandon me, O LORD; my God, do not be far from me.
21.amp: Forsake [azab] me not, O LORD [YHWH]: O my God [Elohim], be not far [rachaq] from me.
21.notes: al-taazbeni YHWH (H5800, H3068): do not ABANDON me, LORD — the verb his strength used on him in verse 10; Elohai al-tirchaq mimmenni (H430, H7368): my God, do not be FAR from me — the distance his kinsmen kept in verse 11. Both losses named in the psalm are handed back to God as things He must not repeat.

22.text: Hurry to my help, O Lord, my salvation.
22.amp: Make haste [chush] to help ['for my help', ezrah, the KJV margin] me, O Lord [Adonai] my salvation [teshuah].
22.notes: chushah le-ezrati (H2363, H5833): HURRY — 'for my help', the margin's literal; Adonai teshuati (H136, H8668): Lord, my salvation. Three short cries close the psalm — do not abandon, do not be far, hurry — and the last word is not the illness or the enemies but teshuah, salvation, which is what He is (cf. Psalm 70:5, whose title is the same single word as this psalm's).
